correctness.rationale: For q>=2,d>=1, the polar of S is exactly the product of coordinate complements A\P_i(S), giving empty closure for empty S, full W if any coordinate support is A, and otherwise the proper Cartesian support box. This proves the exact closed extents/rank polynomial, including q=2 height-two exceptional diamond and d=1 Boolean case. For q>=3,d>=2, two-atom join rank recovers Hamming distance, forcing the full wreath-product automorphisms; an explicit triple violates modularity outside exceptional cases. Binary pair-mixing plus q-letter saturation yields iterative Horn width q, while a full-coordinate line makes width below q impossible; direct width is max(q,d) for q>=3 using coordinate witnesses and matching q-line/private-coordinate minimal stems, while q=2 requires width 2. The source incidence-based checker was inspected; the general proof covers parameters beyond finite test cases.
